items.statement: In colder water systems (65 to 75 °C), eliminate drops and unused piping portions of any length where possible, or apply special sanitizing procedures to them.
items.quote: With colder systems (65 - 75oC), any drops or unused portion of any length of piping has the potential for the formation of a biofilm and should be eliminated if possible or have special sanitizing procedures.

items.statement: Do not use threaded fittings in a pharmaceutical water system.
items.quote: There should be n o threaded fittings in a pharmaceutical water system.

items.statement: Make every pipe joint in the water system either a sanitary fitting or a butt weld.
items.quote: All pipe joints must utilize sanitary fittings or be butt welded.

items.statement: Reverse osmosis may be used to manufacture Water for Injection.
items.quote: Another acceptable method for manufacturing Water for Injection is Reverse Osmosis (RO).

items.statement: Because RO filters are not absolute, install at least two RO units in series.
items.quote: Since RO filters are not absolute, the filter manufacturers recommend that at least two be in series.

items.statement: For WFI systems using PVC or other plastic tubing, have assurance that there are no extractables in addition to testing the water against USP requirements.
items.quote: Looking at the WFI from a system to assure that it meets USP requirements without some assurance that there are no extractables would not be acceptable.

items.statement: Where filters are used in a water system, state each filter's purpose (particulate removal or microbial reduction) and have a procedure setting the filter change frequency based on data from the system validation.
items.quote: If filters are used in a water system there should be a stated purpose for the filter, i.e., particulate removal or microbial reduction, and an SOP stating the frequency with which the filter is to be changed which is based on data generated during the validation of the system.
items.condition: filters used in a water system

items.statement: Take water samples for microbiological testing before the final 0.2 micron filter.
items.quote: Therefore, unless the water is sampled prior to the final 0.2 micron filter, microbiological testing will have little meaning.

items.statement: Drain non-recirculating water systems daily and do not let water sit in the system.
items.quote: This is the reason the agency has recommended that non-recirculating water systems be drained daily and water not be allowed to sit in the system.

items.statement: Where ozone is used to control microbial contamination in a purified water system, keep a dissolved ozone residual in the system for optimum effectiveness.
items.quote: For optimum effectiveness, it is required that dissolved ozone residual remain in the system.

items.statement: During sanitization, crack open the terminal valves so all elbows and bends in the piping fill with water and are fully exposed to the sanitizing agent.
items.quote: During sanitization, it is important to "crack" the terminal valves so that all of the elbows and bends in the piping are full of water and thus, get complete exposure to the sanitizing agent.

items.statement: A one-way (non-recirculating) purified water system may be acceptable if it has good operating procedures based on validation data and routine hot flushing.
items.quote: It should be pointed out that simply because this is a one-way system, it is not inadequate. With good Standard Operational Procedures, based on validation data, and routine hot flushings of this system, it could be acceptable.

items.statement: Maintain UV lights in the water system properly.
items.quote: UV lights must be properly maintained to work.

items.statement: Keep the glass sleeves around UV bulbs clean.
items.quote: The glass sleeves around the bulb(s) must be kept clean or their effectiveness will decrease.

items.statement: In multi-bulb UV units, have a means of determining that each bulb is working.
items.quote: In multibulb units there must be a system to determine that each bulb is functioning.

items.statement: Drug substances may be manufactured using potable water.
items.quote: Currently, the USP, pg. 4, in the General Notices Section, allows drug substances to be manufactured from Potable Water.

items.statement: Manufacture every dosage form with Purified Water, Water for Injection or one of the forms of Sterile Water.
items.quote: It comments that any dosage form must be manufactured from Purified Water, Water For Injection, or one of the forms of Sterile Water.

items.statement: Validate water systems used in the final processing stages of drug substances for parenteral use to assure minimal endotoxin and microbiological contamination.
items.quote: However, such water systems used in the final stages of processing of drug substances for parenteral use should be validated to assure minimal endotoxin/ microbiological contamination.

items.statement: When water microbiological results exceed limits, review the drug product made with that water, basing decisions on its further processing or release on the specific contaminant, the process and the product's end use.
items.quote: Since microbiological test results from a water system are not usually obtained until after the drug product is manufactured, results exceeding limits should be reviewed with regard to the drug product formulated from such water. Consideration with regard to the further processing or release of such a product will be dependent upon the specific contaminant, the process and the end use of the product.

items.statement: When water results exceeding limits affect a drug product, prepare an investigation report that explains the reasoning for release or rejection.
items.quote: It is a good practice for such situations to include an investigation report with the logic for release/rejection discussed in the firm's report.

items.statement: Do not use end-product microbiological testing as the only justification for releasing a drug product, recognizing the limitations of microbiological sampling and testing.
items.quote: End product microbiological testing, while providing some information should not be relied upon as the sole justification for the release of the drug product. The limitations of microbiological sampling and testing should be recognized.

items.statement: Keep maintenance records or logs for water system equipment, such as the still, so that system and equipment problems can be evaluated.
items.quote: Manufacturers should also have maintenance records or logs for equipment, such as the still. These logs should also be reviewed so that problems with the system and equipment can be evaluated.

items.statement: Maintain an accurate description and drawing of the water system so it can be shown to be validated.
items.quote: As pointed out, an accurate description and print of the system is needed in order to demonstrate that the system is validated.
